articles.title: I hoped my children would have epiphanies while visiting my homeland; my father suggested we go swimming instead
articles.summary: I brought my children to Penang to immerse them in the places of their grandparents’ stories. When I stopped lecturing them about gratitude and privilege, we enjoyed our final days doing as locals do.
body: A s I stepped out of Penang international airport, the humidity hit me like I was peering into a just-opened rice cooker. The air carried whiffs of exhaust fumes, fried food and something earthy. It felt thrilling and familiar because I was born in Penang and lived there for six years before I moved to Australia. I looked back at my three children who were visiting for the first time. They were draped over their suitcases like wilted lettuce. “Welcome to Penang,” I said, wiping sweat off my brow.

It was July 2026. It had been 13 years since I last visited Penang, when my father had hosted a lavish wedding dinner featuring a champagne fountain and swan-shaped ice sculpture for me and my new husband. For my white, Australian husband, it was a trip of firsts: his first Chinese tea ceremony; his first 10-course banquet; the first time he met my extended family. But for me, it had been the last time I’d spoken Mandarin and the last time I had seen my grandmother before she died.
points: I brought my children to Penang to immerse them in the places of their grandparents’ stories.
When I stopped lecturing them about gratitude and privilege, we enjoyed our final days doing as locals do.

articles.title: The moment I knew: My late fiance’s favourite song was playing – and Billy said ‘Jamie’s here, isn’t that nice?’
articles.summary: After the death of his partner, Anthony Nocera had almost given up on love. Then Billy walked through the door. Find more stories from the moment I knew series. In 2024, about 18 months after my fiance Jamie passed away, I decided I was lonely and horny and so put myself out there on the apps.
body: I had a guy over for a hook-up one night and he kept fixating on the urn. “So … He’s dead?”
“I hope so,” I said. “Otherwise the urn was a mistake.” “Wow,” he said, not getting the joke. “You’re so brave. I don’t know how you do it.”

Nothing kills a boner faster than someone thinking you’re brave. When someone thinks you’re “brave”, you stop being flesh and pulsing blood and hot salty saliva and start being something coolly observed. Being a “brave widow” makes you desirable in theory. Not practice.

When the urn didn’t ward off potential suitors, my cat Freyja – or Miss Freyja, as Jamie called her – did. She appointed herself my fluffy protector in Jamie’s absence. Each night, she camouflaged herself on the charcoal-grey carpet outside my bedroom and kept watch while I slept. Two emerald eyes scanning for threats.
points: After the death of his partner, Anthony Nocera had almost given up on love.

articles.title: ‘It’s such a joy to ride:’ this cargo e-bike makes errands and commuting a breeze
articles.summary: This pricey ebike is a gamechanger for going around town, getting groceries and hauling cargo with ease – without paying for gas. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things. Parking a car in an urban area can be stressful.
body: An electric bike changes that paradigm – you can roll up on the curb, lock your bike, and walk to your destination. Recently, I tested the Lectric XPedition2, an electric cargo bike that not only made grocery shopping easier but helped me explore my city stress-free.

Like many Aventon or Specialized electrics and other cargo bikes meant for hauling gear, the LectricXPedition2 is a “longtail” bike, meaning there’s a large rack on the back for transporting library books, groceries and even little kids.

The Lectric XPedition2 costs $1,399 which is admittedly much more expensive than an entry-level non-electric bike. Yet, it’s such a joy to ride, so stable and balanced, and lasts so long on a charge that I’ve started driving far less, especially in a downtown area. My daily errands such as coffee runs and shopping are less stressful and more enjoyable.

articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo’s Melting Dress Revives One of Fashion’s Great Runway Experiments
articles.summary: For the opening night of The Unraveled Tour, Rodrigo enlisted the iconic and innovative designer Hussein Chalayan to make a dress that dissolves under water.
body: Olivia Rodrigo has always understood the art of a good fashion reference and a costume change. On the GUTs tour, she had a rotation of slogan tees for the encore that changed from city to city. Her “ drop dead ” music video was jam-packed with sartorial tributes to Sofia Coppola and Jane Birkin. Styled by Chloe and Chenelle Delgadillo, she’s established an on-stage wardrobe rooted in riot grrrl-esque aesthetics and romantic shapes.

On the opening night of The Unraveled Tour, though, Rodrigo swerved the backstage quick-change, wearing a dress that transformed while she was still wearing it. Performing “The Cure” at Hartford’s PeoplesBank Arena on September 25, she appeared in a pristine white collared mini dress with a sweet pleated skirt. Then, as the song reached its climax and Rodrigo repeated, “ I’m unraveled, I’m unraveled...,” artificial rain began to pour from above. The white outer layer started to disintegrate before the audience’s eyes, eventually washing away to reveal a fire-red corseted bodysuit and miniskirt underneath—a pleasingly literal interpretation of the tour’s title.

articles.title: Beauty Marks: The Best Beauty Looks of the Week
articles.summary: Fashion month is in full swing, and the best beauty looks of the week nodded to what’s in store: expect 3D nails, skin-forward glam, and blush, blush, blush!
body: Welcome back to Beauty Marks: Vogue ’s weekly edition of the best moments in celebrity beauty, from Vogue editors’ IG feeds, and all the glam of the fashion and pop culture landscapes. Each week, we curate the nail art to pin for your next nail appointment, new recruits to ‘Team Bob’, and major red carpet moments from the week’s most glamorous affairs. As always, it’s as much about celebrity beauty as it is about the makeup artists, hairstylists, and nail artists, as well as the creators crafting the trends you’re about to see everywhere.

This week, the best beauty looks played with shimmer and metallics: golden eyeshadow that pops, honey-blonde waves, nails glossy and chrome. Take Simone Ashley, for one, whose warm pink blush and glowing contour amped up her already sculptural features. Then there was Florence Pugh, who continues to embrace soft romance with delicate, sumptuously blonde waves tied up with a sweet black ribbon. Fashion Month is in full swing, too, and the beauty details hint at the biggest trends for the season ahead: expect skin-forward complexions, 3D nails, innovative eyeliner, and ’60s vibes.

articles.title: Inside Dove Cameron’s Final Fitting for Her “Celestial” Valentino Wedding Dress in Rome
articles.summary: See a first look at Dove Cameron’s custom Valentino wedding dress here, shared exclusively with Vogue. The musician and actor tied the knot with former Måneskin frontman Damiano David in a ceremony in Tuscany this weekend.
body: Dove Cameron and Damiano David are officially married! As shared exclusively with Vogue, the couple tied the knot this weekend at a private ceremony in Tuscany—and just four days before the wedding weekend celebrations, we joined Dove in Rome to pay a visit to the Valentino ateliers in Rome and try on her wedding dress for the very last time.

“Ciao, Vogue!” the musician and actor says before the final fitting, sitting at an outdoor café and reflecting on the experience of planning the wedding. “I never really dreamed about what my wedding would look like when I was a little girl—I think I wanted to rent out Carnegie Hall and enter in a big, black dress made out of feathers and have a 32-piece orchestra playing,” she says. And while she jokingly describes herself as “wildly unprepared” for the wedding ahead, she also notes: “It feels right. It feels natural. It feels easy. It feels like a natural, beautiful next step. I don't know how else to describe it. I'm in love, [and] we're throwing a big party.”

articles.title: Comedian Edy Modica Is Just Like You (But Funnier)
articles.summary: It’s been a busy few years for Modica, who just released her first stand-up special, “I’m Just Like You (And It Sucks).”
body: When comedian Edy Modica arrives at the Condé Nast offices in downtown Manhattan, she looks as if she’s just wrapped filming on a Bravo show—her hoop earrings are sparkly and huge, her heeled denim boots coordinate perfectly with her long denim shorts, and a nameplate necklace spells out EDY. As I soon learn, that is, in fact, exactly the case; Modica is coming straight from guest-bartending on an episode of Watch What Happens Live With Andy Cohen.

Modica is promoting I’m Just Like You (And It Sucks), her chatty, confrontational, and sometimes crude debut special. (One of its best parts revolves around a young Modica browsing sites with names like “boobs.com” and “sex.com.”) But her strong and singular comedic voice has remained largely unchanged since I saw her perform a fully nude show at Williamsburg’s now-shuttered Annoyance Theatre a decade ago. I struggle with how to bring it up without sounding like a pervert, but Modica excitedly tells me that she remembers the set well; in fact, both of her parents were in attendance.
points: It’s been a busy few years for Modica, who just released her first stand-up special, “I’m Just Like You (And It Sucks).”
